blocks.text: Hitachi Energy India Limited (HEIL) sells the hardware, software and services that move high-voltage electricity from where it is generated to where it is consumed. The disclosed portfolio is transformers (power, traction, dry-type), high-voltage products (gas-insulated and air-insulated switchgear, breakers, bushings, instrument transformers), grid integration (HVDC converter stations, FACTS/STATCOM, power quality), grid automation (SCADA, control and protection, relays) and, from 1 April 2025, a fifth business unit, Service. [F] (AR2026 p.171)

It makes money three ways, and the company reports the split only for third-party domestic orders, not for revenue: **Products 53.4%, Projects 41.3% and Services 5.3% of FY26 third-party domestic orders** (FY25: 52% / 45% / 3%). [F] (AR2026 p.172) The order-mix chart is rendered as a graphic in the filing and the label order is ambiguous in the extracted text; management's own commentary that "our contribution to the products is much higher compared to the projects" supports the reading above. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

On the statutory accounts the revenue split is by accounting timing, not by business unit: sale of products Rs 5,350.29 cr, revenue from execution of project and service contracts Rs 2,351.24 cr, sale of services Rs 216.71 cr and other operating revenue Rs 229.47 cr, totalling Rs 8,147.71 cr in FY26. [F] (AR2026 p.282) **The company reports a single operating segment under Ind AS 108, so there are no segment revenues and no segment margins in the financial statements.** [F] (AR2026 p.282)

Customer profile: utilities and state transmission companies, private renewable developers, industrial captive users (steel, cement, alumina, semiconductors), data-centre developers, Indian Railways and metros, plus Hitachi group companies worldwide. **In FY26 no single customer accounted for more than 10% of revenue; in FY25 Adani Electricity Mumbai Infra Limited did.** [F] (AR2026 p.282) Within exports, Hitachi Energy USA Inc and Hitachi Energy Sweden AB each exceeded 10% of export revenue in both FY26 and FY25. [F] (AR2026 p.282) The company served more than 1,200 customers and booked over 6,800 orders in FY26. [F] (AR2026 p.30-31)

Scale as at 31 March 2026: 19 manufacturing facilities across 8 locations, 13 sales offices, 8 sales touchpoints and 2,777 employees. [F] (AR2026 p.171) A 20th facility at Karjan, Vadodara broke ground on 12 June 2026. [F] (PPT Aug 2026)

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

blocks.text: 1. **The price embeds growth that no disclosed evidence supports.** At Rs 30,200 per share and a market capitalisation of Rs 134,609 cr the stock trades at 117.1x trailing earnings, 94.6x EV/EBITDA and 14.7x EV/sales. [F] (NUMBERS) The reverse DCF says today's enterprise value requires about 120.6% annual sales growth for five years against a base-case equivalent of 13.3%. [F] (NUMBERS) Even allowing for the model's conservative margin input (see Part 4), the absolute multiples are extreme. [AI]

2. **Order intake has been flat for two years while revenue has compounded, so the backlog is being consumed faster than it is refilled at the margin.** Orders were Rs 18,173.8 cr in FY25 and Rs 18,456.5 cr in FY26, growth of 1.6%. [F] (AR2026 p.173) Q1 FY27 orders fell 55.1% YoY to Rs 5,096.5 cr. [F] (PPT Aug 2026) Management's response is to present growth "excluding HVDC", which removes the single largest and lumpiest item from both periods. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [AI]

3. **Roughly nine-tenths of "exports" appear to be sales to Hitachi group entities, not third-party market wins.** Revenue from related parties was Rs 1,928.30 cr in FY26 against total export revenue of Rs 2,134.12 cr. [F] (AR2026 p.282, p.286) Stripping out the two identifiable domestic related parties (Linxon India Rs 21.04 cr and, within "other fellow subsidiaries", Indian group entities) still leaves the overwhelming majority of export revenue intra-group. [E] Management describes a "three-prong" export strategy including third-party sales in allocated markets but has declined to quantify the split: "No, we could not share exact numbers." [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [AI] The economics of a captive feeder factory - management itself calls it "like a low risk and stable margin kind of thing" and "more like a contract with our companies" - do not deserve a differentiated-technology multiple. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

4. **A large and recurring share of profit is paid to the parent for technology the Indian entity does not own.** Royalty and technology fees of Rs 241.85 cr plus Rs 360.59 cr of group IT, engineering, management, legal and professional fees total Rs 602.44 cr in FY26, equal to 7.4% of revenue and 45.6% of profit before tax. [E] from (AR2026 p.286-287) The CFO confirms "we are not spending anything on the R&D. Our R&D spend is all managed centrally." [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) Royalty is reset by the parent and management would not confirm how it is computed on HVDC projects. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [AI] This is a transfer-pricing-exposed cost the minority shareholder does not control.

5. **Cash generation is advance-funded, not earnings-funded, and reverses if ordering pauses.** FY26 cash from operations of Rs 1,244.83 cr was produced with a Rs 2,273.90 cr increase in payables, provisions and other liabilities offsetting a Rs 1,195.62 cr increase in receivables and other assets and a Rs 559.33 cr inventory build. [F] (AR2026 p.238) Customer advances alone rose Rs 1,118.92 cr. [E] from (AR2026 p.283) Working-capital days are -46 in FY26 versus +29 in FY24. [F] (NUMBERS) [AI] A flat order year unwinds this.

6. **The margin gain leans on cost lines that can reverse, and on a non-GAAP margin definition.** Other expenses fell from 20% of revenue in FY25 to 16.9% in FY26 [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) partly because royalty fell in absolute terms (Rs 254.75 cr to Rs 241.85 cr) despite 27.6% revenue growth [F] (AR2026 p.270). The headline "Operational EBITDA" excludes unrealised FX and commodity movements: in Q1 FY27 it excludes a real Rs 36.37 cr unrealised FX loss that is inside reported PBT. [F] (PPT Aug 2026) Our statements data, which does not make that exclusion, shows Q1 FY27 EBITDA of Rs 364 cr against the company's Rs 399.9 cr - the Rs 36 cr gap is almost exactly the excluded FX loss. [E] (NUMBERS)

7. **Capex delivery has repeatedly lagged the stated plan, which undermines the capacity-led growth story.** Against a QIP plan of "Rs 700 plus crores" for FY26 [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), the company added Rs 320.31 cr to capital work in progress [F] (AR2026 p.260) and utilised only Rs 469.66 cr of QIP proceeds, leaving Rs 2,006.48 cr unspent 12 months later. [F] (AR2026 p.291) The auditor reports "certain delays in the utilization of the QIP proceeds". [F] (AR2026 p.231) Rs 98.28 cr of capital work in progress is already overdue against its original plan. [F] (AR2026 p.260)

8. **Governance is structurally minority-unfriendly on the items that matter most.** The promoter holds 71.31% through two nominee directors, the Chairman is a promoter nominee, no director holds a single share, there is no company stock option scheme, and shareholders approved a single related-party contract with Hitachi Energy Sweden AB of up to Rs 2,000 cr for FY26 alone. [F] (AR2026 p.178, p.188, p.213) The transfer pricing study for FY26 was still "in process" at the date the accounts were signed. [F] (AR2026 p.291)

9. **Disclosure on the things an investor most needs is withheld or internally inconsistent.** No installed capacity, no utilisation, no segment margins, no HVDC share of backlog ("we do not give specifically how much is HVDC... We have given enough indications for you to calculate") and no project-level margins. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [F] (AR2026 p.282) The annual report states the Service segment "contributed 71% to the total order book" on the same page cluster where the order break-up shows services at 5.3%. [F] (AR2026 p.171, p.172) These cannot both be right and are not reconciled anywhere. [AI]

10. **New competition is arriving at exactly the point of peak pricing power.** An analyst put it to management that the government is allowing four Chinese players into the GIS and transformer market with a 60-65% local content requirement; management answered "more competition is welcome" and "we do not see any major threat now". [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Crisil independently flags "intense competition" and that "most large orders are procured through competitive bidding, which puts pressure on profitability". [F] (RATING) Management also acknowledges that "despite the supply and demand, there's always an affordability challenge... it's not that whatever price you want, you can get it". [MC] (CALL Nov 2025)

The bear case does not require the business to be bad. It requires only that a high-quality, parent-dependent, utility-exposed equipment maker at 117x trailing earnings is priced for a margin and growth path that management explicitly refuses to guide to. [AI]

blocks.text: Our variant perception is that the market is valuing HEIL as an Indian transmission-capex proxy with an HVDC monopoly, when the disclosed evidence describes something narrower and more dependent: a well-run, cash-rich, 2,777-person Indian manufacturing and project arm of a Swiss-Japanese group, whose technology is licensed rather than owned (Rs 241.85 cr of royalty, zero own R&D), whose exports are overwhelmingly intra-group, whose single largest reported end-market exposure is policy-driven utility ordering (84.6% of domestic third-party orders), and whose two-year order intake has been flat at about Rs 18,400 cr. [F] (AR2026 p.270, p.282, p.286, p.173) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [AI] The operating improvement is real and the backlog is real; what is not evidenced is the step-change in either scale or pricing power that a 117x trailing multiple and a 94.6x EV/EBITDA require. [F] (NUMBERS) The most likely error on the other side is under-weighting how long a 3.5-year backlog plus a doubling of transformer capacity can sustain 20%-plus revenue growth with 15% margins - which would make the current multiple expensive rather than absurd. [E] [AI]

subsections.title: What the timeline reveals about how recent this business really is

blocks.text: The operating assets are old; the corporate entity, the ownership and above all the economics are new. The plants at Maneja, Halol, Savli, Peenya, Doddaballapura, Thandavapura and Chengalpattu came across from ABB India under a 2019 scheme - and the title deeds for Rs 120.86 cr of freehold land and buildings at Maneja and Halol are still, seven years on, held in ABB India Limited's name. [F] (AR2026 p.229, p.256) The Hitachi ownership only became clean in December 2022. [F] (RATING) IT systems were only fully separated from ABB about a year before Q3 FY26: "That we have closed this chapter a year before. Right now, we are totally operating on a standalone basis... we are working on SAP4 HANA." [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

**The profit history that supports today's valuation is essentially two years old.** PAT was Rs 93.9 cr in FY23 and Rs 163.8 cr in FY24 before reaching Rs 384.0 cr in FY25 and Rs 987.8 cr in FY26. [F] (AR2026 p.48) Operational EBITDA margin was 5.7% as recently as FY23. [F] (AR2026 p.48) An investor is therefore extrapolating a two-year margin transition and a one-year backlog step-up (order book up 53.6% in FY26, then up only 10.6% YoY by Q1 FY27) across a five-year forecast horizon. [F] (AR2026 p.14) [F] (PPT Aug 2026) [AI]

sections.title: Business model, production chain and value capture

blocks.text: The company describes its scope as spanning "the entire project lifecycle, including design, engineering, manufacturing, supply, erection, testing, and end-to-end commissioning". [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) The chain, as disclosed, runs as follows.

items: 1. Technology in-licensing. Product designs, architectures, specifications and manufacturing procedures are received from Hitachi Energy Ltd under a royalty and technology fee arrangement; more than 13 technologies were absorbed in FY26 and several are flagged as "not fully absorbed... due to multi-year continuous development plan". [F] (AR2026 p.31, p.221-223)

2. Localisation and engineering. Global designs are adapted to Indian operating conditions, standards and price points. "Local R&D activities undertaken by the Company were mainly in localizing the products, adopting global products for the local environment, carrying out cost saving actions." [F] (AR2026 p.222) Management claims "we produce almost 75%-80% of what we produce globally; we produce locally here" and that local content "is far ahead of the requirements set out". [MC] (CALL Nov 2025, CALL Jun 2026)

3. Sourcing. Raw materials, components and project bought-outs cost Rs 4,618.48 cr in FY26 plus Rs 103.01 cr of stock-in-trade purchases; total purchases were Rs 5,027.11 cr. [F] (AR2026 p.237, p.269) Related-party purchases were Rs 1,349.51 cr, 26% of total purchases, up from 23%. [F] (AR2026 p.286) [F] (AR2026 p.85)

4. Manufacture. 19 facilities across 8 locations - Bengaluru (Peenya, Doddaballapura), Mysuru (Thandavapura), Vadodara (Maneja, Savli main, Savli feeder, Halol, and now Karjan) and Chennai (Chengalpattu). [F] (AR2026 p.202, p.171)
5. Project execution on site. Erection, testing and commissioning, largely for utility and industrial customers; subcontracting charges were Rs 301.27 cr in FY26. [F] (AR2026 p.237)
6. Service and lifecycle. A dedicated Service business unit from 1 April 2025, targeting "a rich installed base" with refurbishment, SCADA upgrades and life-cycle services. [F] (AR2026 p.14, p.32)

7. Export leg. Three routes, per management: allocated markets sold direct; global feeder factories making finished products only made in India (66 kV circuit breakers, COMBIFLEX relays) sold worldwide; and component feeder factories supplying other Hitachi Energy plants in the US, Germany, Sweden and Switzerland. subsections.title: Where value is captured, and why

blocks.text: Value is captured at three points on the disclosed evidence. First, at the qualification barrier: the company powers 9 of India's 18 HVDC links and its solutions run roughly 80% of Indian metro systems, an installed base that is effectively a pre-qualification for the next order and for services. [F] (AR2026 p.171) Second, at the contract structure: management says 60-65% of orders are commodity pass-through with price-variation clauses, so raw-material risk is largely transferred to the customer, while customer advances of Rs 2,723.31 cr fund the working capital. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [F] (AR2026 p.283) Third, at scarcity of delivery slots: management's own capital-expansion risk mitigation is "strategically pre-booking of order slots based on ongoing expansions of the factories", and it tells customers "to order as early as they can". [F] (AR2026 p.41) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

**Value leaks back to the parent in two places.** Rs 241.85 cr of royalty and technology fees and Rs 360.59 cr of group IT, engineering, management, legal and professional charges, together Rs 602.44 cr or 7.4% of revenue in FY26. [E] from (AR2026 p.286-287) Management's position is that this is the price of technology access: "because we are paying the royalty, that is why our SF6-free technology which is available in the world, so we are able to bring it here". [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [AI] The economic reality for a minority shareholder is that the intangible asset sits outside the listed entity and the charge for it is set by the controlling shareholder.

The business is asset-light relative to its revenue but is deliberately becoming heavier. Net property, plant and equipment plus right-of-use assets, CWIP, goodwill and intangibles was Rs 1,037.39 cr against total assets of Rs 12,043.72 cr - 8.6% of the balance sheet. [E] from (AR2026 p.236) Fixed-asset turnover was 9.64x in FY26 against 6.27x in FY23. [F] (NUMBERS) Capex to sales averaged about 2% from FY23 to FY25 before jumping to 6.3% in FY26. [F] (NUMBERS)

Outsourcing is modest: subcontracting charges of Rs 301.27 cr are 3.7% of revenue [E] from (AR2026 p.237), and services from third parties another Rs 88.72 cr. [F] (AR2026 p.270) The heavy lifting is done in-house; the genuine outsourcing is of intellectual property, to the parent. [AI]

Classification: **asset-light today, capital-heavy in transition.** A Rs 4,000 cr cumulative capex commitment against a Rs 845 cr net fixed asset base and Rs 835.45 cr of contracted-but-unprovided capital commitments means the asset base will roughly double before the Karjan plant produces anything in Q4 CY2028. subsections.title: Bottom line: is the improvement structural?

blocks.text: **Partly, and less than the headline suggests.** Roughly two-thirds of the FY26 gain came from cost lines below the gross margin, and three of those are not durable at the same rate:

items: **Royalty fell in absolute terms (Rs 254.75 cr to Rs 241.85 cr) despite 27.6% revenue growth, contributing about 102 bps.** The CFO explains the mechanism: "our royalty expenses are generally dependent upon the previous quarter's revenues". [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) In an accelerating revenue year that lag mechanically depresses royalty as a percentage of current revenue - and it reverses when growth decelerates. This is a timing benefit dressed as an efficiency. [AI]

**The impairment and bad-debt charge halved as a share of revenue (Rs 53.48 cr to Rs 27.58 cr), worth about 50 bps.** [F] (AR2026 p.270) Receivables over three years old are still Rs 150.45 cr and the impairment allowance is still Rs 236.11 cr, 11.0% of gross receivables. [E] from (AR2026 p.264) There is limited room for this line to keep falling. [AI]

**Information technology expenses fell 2.3% in absolute terms, worth about 59 bps.** [F] (AR2026 p.270) The CFO attributes the structural part of this to completing the separation from ABB's IT systems: "we have closed this chapter a year before... we are working on SAP4 HANA. So, we are on our own." [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) That is a genuine one-time saving that cannot repeat. [AI]

blocks.text: What is structural: operating leverage on a genuinely fixed cost base while revenue compounded 27.6%, and the mix shift toward exports and services that management has been executing for two years. Management's own framing has been consistent since at least FY24 and it has delivered ahead of its stated timetable (double-digit operational EBITDA reached before the FY25 target, and double-digit EBIT ahead of the stated Q4 FY26 date). [MC] (CALL Nov 2025, CALL Feb 2026) Crisil expects margins "to further sustain with better operating leverage". [F] (RATING)

**Our read: a sustainable margin corridor in the low-to-mid teens is defensible on this evidence; 16% as a permanent floor is not.** The Q1 FY27 sequential decline (16.4% to 16.0%), the roughly 380 bps YoY gross margin contraction that the CFO initially denied twice before conceding, the reversal risk in royalty, and the input-cost sensitivity in the previous section all argue against extrapolating the peak. [E] [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [AI]

items: **Services mix would have to move up materially.** Services were 5.3% of FY26 third-party domestic orders. **Localisation would have to reduce imported content faster than revenue grows.** In FY26 it did the opposite: foreign exchange used grew 38.9% against 27.6% revenue growth. [E] (AR2026 p.223) Management's stated intent - "the whole idea is to localize more components and to create an end-to-end manufacturing scenario over a period in India" - is the right one, but it is a 2028-and-beyond effect tied to Karjan. **Royalty and group charges would have to scale sub-linearly with revenue.** Management is explicit that royalty is the permanent price of technology access and will continue: "royalty is absolutely required". [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) Group management fees actually rose faster than revenue in FY26 (Rs 84.83 cr to Rs 127.95 cr, +50.8%). [E] (AR2026 p.286)
**Karjan would have to fill quickly.** Two-plus years of construction depreciation and overhead precede any revenue, and there is no disclosed anchor order for the new capacity. [AI]

**Pricing would have to hold as Chinese, Korean and Mexican competition and new domestic capacity arrive.** Management's own words: "Various companies have announced the capacity expansion. Considering the existing capacities plus capacities to come, we believe that still there is a gap to close on." [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)
All analysis is standalone. The company had no subsidiary, associate or joint venture in FY26, so there are no consolidated accounts to cross-check. [F] (AR2026 p.231)

[F] (NUMBERS) Over the same period the asset base barely moved. That is a one-time repair of a depressed cost structure, not a repeatable compounding engine. [AI]

**Missed on the bull side: the margin floor may be higher than the model assumes.** Every scenario in our DCF uses 5-11%; the company has delivered 15.4% and 16.0%. [F] (NUMBERS), [F] (AR2026 p.48) If low-to-mid teens proves to be the floor, the entire valuation frame in this report is too conservative.

**Missed on the bear side: the export story is a group-allocation story.** The market appears to read 26% export revenue as third-party competitive success; the related-party note suggests otherwise, and management's own description of the largest leg is "a pass-through... low risk and stable margin". [E] (AR2026 p.282, p.286) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

**Missed on the bear side: the FY26 margin gain is partly a royalty timing artefact.** Royalty is charged on prior-quarter revenue, so accelerating growth mechanically depresses it as a percentage of current revenue - worth about 102 basis points in FY26 on our decomposition - and it reverses when growth slows. [E] (AR2026 p.270) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) This has never been raised on any call.

**Missed on both sides: nobody has asked what the 2029 capacity is actually worth.** Management gives 30-40 GVA and Rs 4,000 cr; nobody has asked for revenue per GVA, and without it the capacity story cannot be valued at all. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [AI]

**The other half is genuine.** 117.1x trailing earnings, 94.6x EV/EBITDA, 14.7x EV/sales and 26.01x book are extreme on any framework, including one that fully credits the current margin. [F] (NUMBERS) They imply that the FY26 margin is permanent, that order intake re-accelerates from a two-year plateau, that Rs 4,000 cr of capacity fills on arrival in 2029, and that data centres and BESS convert into disclosed revenue. [AI]

**A third factor is scarcity.** There are very few listed ways to own Indian high-voltage grid infrastructure with a AAA balance sheet, a global technology parent and 3.5 years of backlog cover. Scarcity premia are real and no discounted cash flow captures them - but they are also the first thing to compress when the growth rate normalises. [AI]

subsections.title: Investment horizon and when to re-review

blocks.text: **Horizon.** This is not a security whose thesis resolves in a quarter. The two events that would materially change the evidence base are the HVDC award management expects by around February 2027 and the Karjan commissioning in Q4 CY2028. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), [F] (PPT Aug 2026) An investor underwriting the structural case needs a three-to-five-year horizon and the willingness to sit through a 52-week range that has already spanned Rs 16,104 to Rs 38,800. [F] (NUMBERS) An investor underwriting the current multiple needs, on the evidence in this report, something the company has declined to provide: a forecast.

blocks.text: **Research view, stated plainly and without a rating.** Hitachi Energy India is a genuinely strong operating business - entrenched, cash-rich, AAA-rated, with a backlog covering three and a half years of revenue and a margin that has tripled in three years - attached to a valuation that every model in this evidence pack says is between twelve and sixty times fair value, and attached to a parent that owns the technology, sets the royalty, allocates the export markets and holds 71.31% of the votes. The operating case and the price are not the same question, and an investor should answer them separately. [F] (NUMBERS), [F] (AR2026 p.171, p.291) [AI]

**No previous report exists for this company in this dashboard, so this is initial coverage and there is no prior-quarter comparison to make.** The baseline established here is: share price Rs 30,200 and market capitalisation Rs 134,609 cr; trailing twelve-month sales Rs 9,162 cr, EBITDA Rs 1,424 cr and PAT Rs 1,150 cr; FY26 revenue Rs 8,147.71 cr, operational EBITDA margin 15.4% and PAT Rs 987.84 cr; Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 2,493.7 cr, operational EBITDA margin 16.0% and PAT Rs 294.2 cr; order intake Rs 5,096.5 cr in the quarter and Rs 18,456.5 cr in FY26; order backlog Rs 32,222.1 cr at 30 June 2026; cash Rs 4,689.17 cr against borrowings of Rs 86 cr; promoter holding 71.31%. [F] (NUMBERS), [F] (AR2026 p.237, p.48, p.173), [F] (PPT Aug 2026) The guidance tracker in Part 3 is the baseline against which next quarter's delivery should be tested, and the monitoring dashboard in this part lists the twelve metrics to carry forward. [AI]

One prior input did exist: this dashboard's earlier research notes, which characterised HVDC as the moat, flagged import substitution as a policy tailwind, and warned that "at 128x earnings this is the most demanding valuation on the board by a distance", that revenue is concentrated in policy-driven utility customers, that DII holding had fallen from 12.34% to 6.32% while FII rose, and that the promoter stake had stepped down from 75% to 71.31%. [BOARD] **This report confirms every one of those observations against source documents, and adds three the notes did not capture: that roughly 90% of export revenue appears to be intra-group, that Rs 602.44 cr of royalty and group service charges equal 45.6% of pre-tax profit, and that order intake has been flat for two years.** [E] (AR2026 p.282, p.286-287, p.173) [AI] The notes' own caveat - that the narrow global HVDC supplier set "was not verified against an external source in this pass" - still stands; nothing in this evidence pack verifies it either. [BOARD]

**Unit economics** - no capacity, volume or realisation data exists, so only per-employee and per-order proxies could be built. **Competitive landscape** - no peer set is disclosed anywhere, so no peer multiple or margin comparison was possible and none was imported. **Segments** - single-segment reporting means no segment revenue or margin analysis could be performed. **Capacity** - the facility map has empty capacity and utilisation columns throughout. **FY23 and FY24 order intake** - read from a bar chart and labelled as such. **Director ages and appointment dates** - not disclosed. **Prospectus and QIP placement document** - referenced repeatedly by management but not available in this evidence pack

summary.one_line: Hitachi Energy India is an entrenched, debt-free, AAA-rated Indian grid-equipment incumbent with a Rs 32,222 cr order backlog covering about 3.5 years of revenue and a margin that has tripled in three years - but order intake has been flat for two years, roughly nine-tenths of its export revenue appears to be intra-group, Rs 602 cr of royalty and group charges equal 45.6% of pre-tax profit, and at 117x trailing earnings the price sits far above every fair value our DCF produces.
bull_points: Record, audited order backlog of Rs 32,222.1 cr at 30 June 2026, up 10.6% YoY and 9.0% QoQ, equal to about 3.5x trailing twelve-month sales of Rs 9,162 cr and disclosed as remaining performance obligations converting over 1 to 5 years. [F] (PPT Aug 2026), [F] (AR2026 p.283), [E] (NUMBERS)

The margin has structurally re-rated: operational EBITDA margin went from 5.7% in FY23 to 9.3% in FY25 to 15.4% in FY26 and 16.0% in Q1 FY27, with PAT up 2.6x in FY26 to Rs 987.84 cr. [F] (AR2026 p.48), [F] (PPT Aug 2026)

Documented incumbency that is hard to displace: the company powers 9 of India's 18 HVDC links, its transformers support 1 in 3 Indian Railways locomotives, about 80% of Indian metro systems run on its solutions, and it connects over 60 GW of renewables. [F] (AR2026 p.171)

Fortress balance sheet and self-funded growth: zero borrowings, Rs 4,689.17 cr of cash, Crisil AAA/Stable reaffirmed with A1+ reassigned on Rs 6,000 cr of facilities at zero fund-based utilisation, and a -42 day cash conversion cycle. [F] (AR2026 p.236), [F] (RATING), [F] (NUMBERS)

Capacity is being roughly doubled with committed funding: Rs 4,000 cr cumulative capex, a greenfield Karjan plant adding 30-40 GVA and internalising HVDC converter transformers for the first time, targeted for December 2028 and paid for from a completed Rs 2,520.82 cr equity raise. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026), [F] (PPT Aug 2026), [F] (AR2026 p.239)
bear_points: The valuation leaves no room for error: 117.1x trailing earnings, 94.6x EV/EBITDA, 14.7x EV/sales and 26.01x book, against a DCF bear-base-bull range of Rs 485.5 to Rs 2,455.4 per share and a reverse DCF that implies about 120.6% annual sales growth for five years versus a 13.3% base-case equivalent. [F] (NUMBERS)

Order intake has been flat for two years - Rs 18,173.8 cr in FY25 and Rs 18,456.5 cr in FY26, growth of 1.6% - and fell 55.1% YoY in Q1 FY27; management's preferred metric removes HVDC from both periods. [F] (AR2026 p.173), [F] (PPT Aug 2026), [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Roughly 90% of export revenue appears to be intra-group: related-party revenue of Rs 1,928.30 cr against total export revenue of Rs 2,134.12 cr, with no third-party split ever disclosed and management describing the largest export leg as "a pass-through... low risk and stable margin". [E] (AR2026 p.282, p.286), [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Rs 241.85 cr of royalty plus Rs 360.59 cr of group service charges - Rs 602.44 cr, 7.4% of revenue and 45.6% of pre-tax profit - flow to the controlling shareholder, the company spends nothing on its own R&D, and the FY26 transfer pricing study was still "in process" when the accounts were signed. [E] (AR2026 p.286-287, p.291), [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

About two-thirds of the FY26 margin gain came from below the gross margin, including roughly 102 basis points from a royalty bill that fell in absolute terms only because royalty is charged on prior-quarter revenue - a timing benefit that reverses when growth slows - and 18.2% of pre-tax profit is deposit interest on undeployed QIP cash that management says will fall. [E] (AR2026 p.270, p.268), [MC] (CALL Nov 2025)
watch_points: Order intake excluding HVDC in Q2 FY27 (results expected early November 2026): whether the +26.1% YoY ex-HVDC growth of Q1 FY27 holds, and whether the two-year plateau in reported intake of about Rs 18,400 cr finally breaks. [F] (PPT Aug 2026), [F] (AR2026 p.173)
